stories.headline: After Bowers and The Mouse Rats Meet at 10-10 With Sixth Place on the Line
stories.dek: Ezra added Saquon Barkley on Friday, a day before the two teams tied at the playoff line face off in Week 11.
body: The race for the last playoff spot runs straight through one game this weekend. Ezra's After Bowers and Bryar's The Mouse Rats are both 10-10, sitting sixth and seventh in the standings, and they play each other in Week 11, with four weeks left in the regular season.

Ezra made his move before kickoff. On Friday, After Bowers sent Stefon Diggs and Jordan Mason to Jared's I want my Nickleback for running back Saquon Barkley, the 16th trade of the season. Barkley scored 55.2 points in seven starts for Jared. Diggs had 39.2 points for After Bowers and Mason 14.7.

The two teams arrive in different form. After Bowers have averaged 120.6 points over the last three weeks, posted the league's best score of Week 10 at 145.9 and climbed to fifth in the power rankings. The Mouse Rats have averaged 89.1 over the same stretch and sit eighth in the rankings, up one spot. For the season, After Bowers lead in points, 1069.2 to 973.0. Bryar holds the all-time series, 4-0.

The projections lean the other way this week: The Mouse Rats at 110.7, After Bowers at 95.4. After Bowers already have 7.3 points on the board from two finished starters, while The Mouse Rats have all nine still to play. Dak Prescott (21.9 projected) and George Pickens lead the After Bowers group against Tennessee at 1 p.m. Sunday, and Chase Brown plays Monday night. Patrick Mahomes (21.8) and Derrick Henry go at 1 p.m. for The Mouse Rats.

The median game matters just as much. The projected median sits at 105.0, which puts The Mouse Rats 5.7 points above the line and After Bowers 9.6 below it. If one side wins both games and the other loses both, the gap between them becomes two games.

Others are close enough to benefit. Garrett's Every Inch Matters are 9-11 and projected to trail The House Cats 106.1 to 95.8. Tyler's Breece's Pieces sit one game above the pack at 11-9 and face first-place Lisan al Gibbs. Next week, After Bowers visit Breece's Pieces.

stories.headline: Lisan al Gibbs Open Up a 22-Point Lead on Breece's Pieces
stories.dek: C.J. Stroud and the Texans defense put Josh ahead early, but Tyler still has Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase waiting for Monday night.
body: Josh's Lisan al Gibbs did not wait for Sunday. With two starters finished, the 18-2 leaders have a 35.5 to 13.3 lead on Tyler's Breece's Pieces, and they are projected to win 133.1 to 116.7. It is the top seed against the fifth seed, in a series the two managers have split 3-3.

Most of the early damage came from Houston. C.J. Stroud scored 20.5 points at quarterback and the Texans D/ST added 15.0, the two best individual games of the week so far. Nico Collins accounts for all 13.3 of Breece's Pieces' points, the fourth-best score from the games already played.

Plenty is left. Lisan al Gibbs have seven starters still to play, led by Jahmyr Gibbs at home against Tampa Bay at 1 p.m. Sunday. Gibbs has scored 232.9 points in nine starts, the most of any player for any team this season, and he is projected for 19.8. Tony Pollard (17.0) and D'Andre Swift (15.6) also play in the early window.

Breece's Pieces have eight starters left, and their two biggest projections land last. Joe Burrow (22.9) and Ja'Marr Chase (21.1) play at Washington at 8:15 p.m. Monday. Bucky Irving (16.0) is on the other side of the Gibbs game in Detroit on Sunday. Lisan al Gibbs also have Tee Higgins in that Monday game.

The stakes are not even. Lisan al Gibbs carry a six-game win streak and lead the league in points with 1238.9. Breece's Pieces are 11-9 after an 0-2 Week 10 and sit one game ahead of the two 10-10 teams. Their remaining opponents average 112.6 points per game, the third-toughest schedule left in the league.
Tyler won the title in 2023 and 2025. Josh has made the playoffs twice in three past seasons. A Breece's Pieces comeback would need the Monday night duo at their best.

stories.headline: George Kittle Lines Up Against Jeremy's Team After This Week's Trade
stories.dek: I want my Nickleback lead Illegal use of hands early, and Jared's newest additions get a crack at the teams that sent them away.
body: This week's trade gets an early test. Jared's I want my Nickleback host Jeremy's Illegal use of hands in Week 11, days after Jeremy sent George Kittle and Kyren Williams to Jared for Josh Jacobs. With one starter finished on each side, Nickleback lead 13.9 to 4.2, and they are projected to win 104.0 to 91.6.

Kittle is in Jared's starting lineup for Sunday night against Minnesota, projected for 10.7 points. He scored 87.5 points while starting for Illegal use of hands before the deal. Stefon Diggs, acquired from After Bowers on Friday, starts too, playing Monday night against Cincinnati alongside quarterback Jayden Daniels, projected for 19.6.

David Montgomery supplied all 13.9 of Nickleback's points so far. Illegal use of hands have eight starters left, with Trevor Lawrence (19.5) and Bhayshul Tuten (15.9) both playing at the Giants at 4:25 p.m. Sunday.

The records point one way and the history points the other. Illegal use of hands are 14-6 and second in the standings, though they have dropped two straight games. I want my Nickleback are 3-17 with a nine-game losing streak. Jared, though, is 3-0 all-time against Jeremy.

The median adds a second layer. Illegal use of hands finished 1.6 points short of it last week, and this week's projection has them 13.4 below the projected median of 105.0. Nickleback are projected 1.0 below it, the closest team to the line from either side. The House Cats sit 1.1 above it.
Jared has made 10 trades this season, the most in the league. Lisan al Gibbs already lead Illegal use of hands by four games for the top seed, and The Silly Geese are one game behind Jeremy at 13-7.

stories.headline: The House Cats Spend $17 on Bo Nix, the Week's Biggest Waiver Bid
stories.dek: Nix lands on his second BBFC roster in five days, and eight paid claims cost the league $52 in all.
body: Luke made the biggest move of the Week 11 waiver run. The House Cats put in a $17 claim for quarterback Bo Nix on Wednesday and dropped tight end Mike Gesicki to make room. Nix goes straight into the starting lineup, projected for 20.8 points when Denver hosts Las Vegas at 4:25 p.m. Sunday. No other bid this week topped $10.

Nix has been on the move. He sat on the Lisan al Gibbs bench in Week 9 and scored 15.7 points there. Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun picked him up as a free agent on Nov. 14, then released him a day later to add Drew Lock. Gesicki was a short stay as well; The House Cats had added him as a free agent on Nov. 14.

Eight claims cost money this week, $52 in all. Garrett's Every Inch Matters paid $10 for tight end Mark Andrews without dropping anyone. Jeremy's Illegal use of hands spent $7 on the Rams D/ST and released the 49ers D/ST. Tyler's Breece's Pieces gave $5 for the Ravens D/ST, and Michael's The Silly Geese paid $4 for the Panthers D/ST. Both defenses start Sunday, on opposite sides of Baltimore's game at Carolina. Bryar's The Mouse Rats claimed running back Mike Washington Jr. for $2.

No one was busier than Caleb. Pteem Shteevenshun made five moves, more than any other team: $5 for receiver Xavier Hutchinson, $2 for running back Emari Demercado, and free-agent adds of the Chargers D/ST, J.K. Dobbins and Aaron Rodgers. Demercado went back out the same day to open a spot for Rodgers, and Dobbins replaced Austin Ekeler. Rodgers, Hutchinson and the Chargers D/ST are all in this week's lineup, with Rodgers projected for 15.1 points. Hutchinson plays tonight when Houston hosts Indianapolis.

The season totals keep climbing at the top. Every Inch Matters have now spent $96, second only to Jared's $100, and their 84 pickups lead the league by a wide margin. The Mouse Rats are next with 55. At the other end, Landon's GAYleb williams have spent $32 and Jeremy's team $37, and they sit fourth and second in the standings.

stories.headline: Kenneth Walker III Tops the Season's Trade Returns as the Deadline Nears
stories.dek: Fifteen trades in, September's deals have paid off the most, and Walker carries the league's top projection into Sunday.
body: With 13 days left before the Dec. 2 trade deadline, the best return on any BBFC trade this season still belongs to a September deal. Kenneth Walker III has scored 109.7 points in five starts for Garrett's Every Inch Matters since arriving from Jared's I want my Nickleback on Sept. 29. He had scored 53.4 for Nickleback before the move.

Jared did well out of the same trade. Jayden Daniels has 103.6 points in five starts for Nickleback, after 32.4 with Every Inch Matters, and leads Jared's roster in points while started. Tee Higgins came over in that deal too and scored 48.2 for Nickleback before Jared sent him to Josh's Lisan al Gibbs on Oct. 29. Higgins has 59.3 points in three starts for his new team.

Three other players have topped 60 points for the teams that traded for them. Joe Burrow has given Tyler's Breece's Pieces 77.9 in three starts since a Sept. 29 deal with Micah's Real Man of Genius. Patrick Mahomes has 68.4 in four starts for Bryar's The Mouse Rats since an Oct. 16 trade with The Silly Geese, and Michael Wilson has 63.9 in six starts for Every Inch Matters since an Oct. 2 deal with The Silly Geese. Micah's side of the Burrow trade has held up as well, with Travis Kelce at 44.7 points in six starts and Aaron Jones Sr. at 40.1 in four.

Jared has been part of nine of the season's 15 trades, including the newest, which sent Kyren Williams and George Kittle to Nickleback for Josh Jacobs this week. The two sides meet this week. Kittle is in Nickleback's lineup with a 10.7-point projection, and Nickleback are projected to win 103.3 to 90.6. Michael's The Silly Geese have made six trades. Landon's GAYleb williams and Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun have yet to make one.

Walker heads into Week 11 with the highest projection of any starter in the league, 24.1 points. Every Inch Matters visit Luke's The House Cats and are projected to win 112.8 to 105.3. At 9-11, they are one game behind After Bowers and The Mouse Rats, who are tied for sixth at 10-10.

stories.headline: Lisan al Gibbs Reach 18 Wins With Four Weeks Still to Play
stories.dek: Their 18-2 mark already equals Josh's full 2025 win total, and Week 11 brings Tyler, the two-time champion.
body: Josh's Lisan al Gibbs are 18-2 with four weeks left in the regular season. That is already as many wins as Josh collected in all 28 games of 2025, when he went 18-10, and two shy of the 20-8 record that made Jeremy last season's top seed. Median games count in both records.

Both losses came in the same week. In Week 4, Landon's GAYleb williams beat Lisan al Gibbs 126.9 to 97.4, and the 97.4 fell short of that week's 109.8 median. They have won every game since, six straight head to head and six straight against the median, and they are 9-1 in both columns.

The scoring backs it up. Lisan al Gibbs lead the league with 1,238.9 points, 123.9 a game, and have averaged 127.7 over the last three weeks. Their 162.6 in Week 5 is still the highest score of the season. Jahmyr Gibbs has 232.9 points in nine starts, the most of any player in the league, and the team sits first in the power rankings with a 93.4 score, the top mark in record, scoring and form.

History offers a caution. Josh has never won a title, going 33-23 across three past seasons with two playoff trips. He was the No. 4 seed in both 2024 and 2025 and finished sixth each time. The top seed has not won the championship in any of the league's three past seasons: Jared finished fourth from the top spot in 2023, Bryar second in 2024 and Jeremy second in 2025. Tyler won it all in 2023 as the No. 6 seed with a 6-8 record.

Tyler is next. His Breece's Pieces host Lisan al Gibbs in Week 11, and the all-time series stands at 3-3. ESPN projects Josh's team to win 126.1 to 116.6. C.J. Stroud and the Texans D/ST get Lisan al Gibbs started tonight against Indianapolis. Their remaining opponents average 102.9 points a game. After Tyler comes Micah's Real Man of Genius in Week 12, a series Josh leads 4-1.

stories.headline: Jeremy Sends Kyren Williams and George Kittle to Jared for Josh Jacobs
stories.dek: The No. 2 seed moves two regular starters for Jacobs days before the two clubs meet in Week 11, and around the league the early verdict favors Jared.
body: The 15th trade of the season came together Tuesday morning. Jeremy's Illegal use of hands, second in the standings at 14-6, sent running back Kyren Williams and tight end George Kittle to Jared's I want my Nickleback for running back Josh Jacobs. The deal was accepted at 11:25 a.m. It is Jeremy's first trade of the year and Jared's ninth, the most in the league. The Silly Geese are next with six.
The early reviews are in, and they lean one way. The general consensus around the league is that Jared won the trade handily.

Williams has been a fixture for Illegal use of hands. He started all 10 weeks and scored 145.3 points in the lineup, second on the team behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 223.7. His best day was 31.7 in Week 4. The last three weeks were quieter at 12.4, 7.6 and 4.2, each below his ESPN projection. Kittle started seven times at tight end, in Weeks 3 through 7 and again in Weeks 9 and 10, and scored 87.5 points, or 12.5 a start, with a high of 23.2 in Week 3.

Jacobs has three starts this season, all for Nickleback, in Weeks 7 through 9: 17.6, 20.2 and 0.5 points. He sat on the bench without an ESPN projection in Weeks 1 through 6 and again in Week 10, and ESPN currently lists him as out.

Illegal use of hands makes the move with its playoff place close to settled. The site's playoff odds have it above 99 percent to make the field and at 68 percent for one of the two first-round byes. Its 1,233.54 points are second in the league, 5.36 behind Lisan al Gibbs, though it has gone 1-3 over the last two weeks. Nickleback is 3-17 and 12th after nine straight losses, and the odds show it needs a 2-0 week to stay alive.

That 2-0 week would have to come against Jeremy. Nickleback hosts Illegal use of hands in Week 11, so the two sides of the deal meet right away, and Jared is 3-0 against Jeremy all time, playoffs included. Jared won the 2024 title, and Jeremy finished second to Tyler last season. The trade deadline is Dec. 2.

stories.headline: Week 10 Leaves Two Teams Tied for Sixth With Four Weeks to Play
stories.dek: After Bowers and The Mouse Rats both went 2-0 to reach 10-10, and the two meet head to head in Week 11.
body: Week 10 is in the books, and the playoff line is more crowded than it was a week ago. After Bowers and The Mouse Rats each went 2-0 and now sit at 10-10, sixth and seventh, with After Bowers holding the last playoff seed. Every Inch Matters also swept its two games and is one game back at 9-11. Four weeks remain in the regular season.

Ezra's After Bowers beat Landon's GAYleb williams 145.9 to 117.1, the highest score of the week, behind George Pickens (38.0) and Dak Prescott (34.4). Bryar's The Mouse Rats beat Tyler's Breece's Pieces 117.2 to 105.7, led by Patrick Mahomes with 35.4 and Parker Washington with 24.7. Both winners cleared the week's median of 113.5. Garrett's Every Inch Matters beat Real Man of Genius 123.2 to 75.0.

Breece's Pieces had the hardest week of the bubble teams. Its 105.7 fell short of the median, so Tyler went 0-2 and ended a three-game head-to-head winning streak. Ja'Marr Chase led the lineup with 28.6, while Joe Burrow scored 33.2 on the bench. Breece's Pieces is still fifth at 11-9, a game ahead of the 10-10 pair, but slipped from fifth to sixth in the power rankings as After Bowers moved up from sixth to fifth.

The top of the table held. Josh's Lisan al Gibbs beat The Silly Geese 133.9 to 115.0 to reach 18-2 on a six-game winning streak. Illegal use of hands is second at 14-6, The Silly Geese third at 13-7 and GAYleb williams fourth at 12-8. Below the line, Pteem Shteevenshun and Real Man of Genius are 7-13, The House Cats 6-14 and I want my Nickleback 3-17.

Week 11 puts the two 10-10 teams in the same game. The Mouse Rats host After Bowers, who are projected to win 106.7 to 94.3, while Bryar is 4-0 against Ezra all time. Every Inch Matters visits The House Cats with a 111.8 to 78.6 projection, and Breece's Pieces hosts Lisan al Gibbs, projected to lose 126.3 to 105.4 in a series tied 3-3. The schedules split from there: After Bowers' remaining opponents average 96.2 points per game and The Mouse Rats' 99.5, against 112.6 for Breece's Pieces and a league-high 114.4 for Every Inch Matters.

stories.headline: Every Inch Matters Posts Week 10's Biggest Margin and Climbs to 9-11
stories.dek: Garrett's team beat Real Man of Genius by 48.2 points and has gone 4-0 over the last two weeks to sit one game out of sixth.
body: Garrett's Every Inch Matters put up the widest margin of Week 10, beating Micah's Real Man of Genius 123.2 to 75.0. The 48.2-point win and a third-place weekly score gave Garrett a second straight 2-0 week. Every Inch Matters was 5-11 after Week 8 and is now 9-11, one game behind the two teams tied for sixth.

Two players carried the lineup. Emmett Johnson scored 32.1 points in his first start for Every Inch Matters since arriving from The Silly Geese in an October 2 trade. Brock Purdy added 31.7, bringing him to 153.4 points in seven starts this season. Antonio Williams' 11.2 was the best score on the bench, which totaled 18.2.

The turnaround has been steady. In Week 7, Every Inch Matters scored 52.8, still the lowest total by any team this season. Since then Garrett is 5-1: a win over The Mouse Rats in Week 8, then two-win weeks against After Bowers and Real Man of Genius. The team has averaged 108.1 points over the last three weeks, compared with 98.0 for the season.

Real Man of Genius drops to 7-13 after the loss. Deebo Samuel Sr. led Micah's starters with 24.4 and Tyler Shough added 10.0, while Ryan Flournoy scored 16.1 on the bench. Micah's team is tied with Pteem Shteevenshun at 7-13, three games out of sixth with four weeks left.

The road ahead is the hardest in the league for Every Inch Matters. Its remaining opponents average 114.4 points per game, the highest of any team, and it ranks 10th in the power rankings despite the recent run. Week 11 starts with a trip to The House Cats, where Every Inch Matters is projected to win 111.8 to 78.6 and Garrett leads Luke 2-1 all time. Week 12 brings Illegal use of hands, a series Jeremy leads 3-2.

stories.headline: Illegal Use of Hands Wins Its Game but Misses the Median by 1.6
stories.dek: Week 10's median of 113.5 was the season's second-highest, and four teams split their two games in unusual fashion.
body: Jeremy's Illegal use of hands beat The House Cats 111.9 to 101.4 and still came away with a 1-1 week. The median landed at 113.5, and Illegal use of hands finished seventh in the weekly scoring, 1.6 points below the line. It was only the third median loss of the season for Jeremy's team, which stands 7-3 head to head and 7-3 against the median.

The bar was high. Only Week 5's median of 116.2 has been higher this season, while the lowest, in Week 2, was 91.8. Six teams cleared it: After Bowers at 145.9, Lisan al Gibbs at 133.9, Every Inch Matters at 123.2, The Mouse Rats at 117.2, GAYleb williams at 117.1 and The Silly Geese at 115.0. The cut fell between The Silly Geese and Illegal use of hands, a gap of 3.2 points.

Two teams lost head to head and still won the median. Michael's The Silly Geese fell 133.9 to 115.0 to Lisan al Gibbs but finished 1.6 points above the line. Landon's GAYleb williams lost by 28.8 to After Bowers, and its 117.1 was enough for a median win that moves Landon to 7-3 against the median this season.

Two others won head to head and lost the median. Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun beat I want my Nickleback 104.2 to 73.8, a 30.4-point margin, but finished 9.3 points below the median. The Rams D/ST led Caleb's lineup with 16.0 and Bijan Robinson added 15.7. Pteem Shteevenshun is 3-7 against the median, tied with Real Man of Genius and The House Cats for the fewest median wins outside last place.

For Illegal use of hands, Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 27.1 and Trevor Lawrence 26.8. Isaiah Likely put up 23.2 on the bench. Jeremy's team is still second at 14-6, one game ahead of The Silly Geese. Week 11 brings a trip to I want my Nickleback, and the projection is close at 98.9 to 98.1 for Illegal use of hands. Jared is 3-0 against Jeremy all time.

stories.headline: Ravens-Chargers Holds the Last Open Questions of Week 10
stories.dek: Three BBFC starters play Monday night, and one of them will settle the week's closest matchup and its final median spot.
body: Nine of Week 10's twelve lineups are finished, and everything left to decide runs through one NFL game. Baltimore hosts the Chargers at 8:15 p.m. Monday with three BBFC starters on the field: Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers and the Ravens D/ST. Henry is the one with the most riding on him.

Tyler's Breece's Pieces finished Sunday with 105.7 points. Bryar's The Mouse Rats sit at 100.7 with Henry still to play, a gap of 5.0 points. Henry is projected for 17.6, which would put The Mouse Rats at 118.3. Breece's Pieces came into the week on a three-game winning streak, while Tyler is 0-3 against Bryar in their all-time series.

Henry also controls the last median spot. The current median is 108.8, the midpoint between Jeremy's Illegal use of hands in sixth at 111.9 and Breece's Pieces in seventh at 105.7. Illegal use of hands is finished, so if Henry scores 11.2 points or more, The Mouse Rats move past them and take the sixth median win. On projections, the median rises to 113.5, with Illegal use of hands 1.6 points short. Breece's Pieces cannot climb back into the top six on Monday.

The other two Ravens starters are protecting leads. Josh's Lisan al Gibbs leads Michael's The Silly Geese 125.5 to 115.0, and The Silly Geese have no one left to play. Flowers is projected for 11.9, which would lift Lisan al Gibbs to 137.4. Garrett's Every Inch Matters leads Micah's Real Man of Genius 119.2 to 75.0, with the Ravens D/ST, projected for 7.8, still to go.

The standings stakes are real at both ends. Lisan al Gibbs entered the week at 16-2, three games clear of Illegal use of hands at 13-5, and Jeremy's median result now waits on a player from another team. Near the cut line, Ezra's After Bowers holds the sixth seed at 8-10, level with The Mouse Rats in seventh, and After Bowers already owns the week's top score at 145.9. Breece's Pieces, fifth at 11-7, will be watching Henry for its head-to-head result.

stories.headline: After Bowers Posts 145.9, Its Best Score of the Season by Nearly 25 Points
stories.dek: Dak Prescott and George Pickens combined for 72.4 points as Ezra's lineup built a 28.8-point lead over GAYleb williams.
body: Ezra's After Bowers had not topped 121 points all season. On Sunday it put up 145.9, the highest score of Week 10, and its lineup is finished with a 28.8-point lead over Landon's GAYleb williams. The total beats After Bowers' previous high of 120.9, set in a Week 5 loss to The Silly Geese, by nearly 25 points.

Two players did most of the work. George Pickens scored 38.0 points and Dak Prescott added 34.4, a combined 72.4, or close to half of the team's total. Prescott has been After Bowers' most productive player all year, with 167.4 points in nine starts through Week 9. Pickens' 38.0 is the third-best individual score of the week so far, behind only Christian McCaffrey and Jahmyr Gibbs.

The number holds up against the whole season. Only three scores this year have been higher: Lisan al Gibbs' 162.6 in Week 5, The Mouse Rats' 149.1 in Week 1 and Illegal use of hands' 148.9 in Week 6. After Bowers had averaged 102.6 points per game coming in and sat sixth in the power rankings.

GAYleb williams did not have a bad day. Its 117.1 points rank fourth this week and sit 8.3 above the current median of 108.8, which puts Landon in position for a median win even with the head-to-head out of reach. Landon came in on a three-game winning streak at 11-7, the fourth seed, and trailed Ezra 1-3 in their all-time series.

The timing matters for After Bowers. Ezra entered the week holding the sixth and final playoff seed at 8-10, with a 3-6 head-to-head mark and a 5-4 record against the median. If the lead and the top-six score both hold through Monday night, After Bowers would reach 10-10 with four weeks left in the regular season.

stories.headline: McCaffrey's 44.3 Leads a Sunday of Big Individual Games
stories.dek: Jahmyr Gibbs, Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson also cleared 30 points, though not every big day came with a lead.
body: Christian McCaffrey turned in the best individual game of Week 10 so far, scoring 44.3 points for Luke's The House Cats. It was not quite enough. The House Cats finished at 101.4, and Jeremy's Illegal use of hands, also done for the week, sits 10.5 points ahead at 111.9 with nothing left to play on either side.

McCaffrey came into the week with 148.7 points in eight starts, the most on the House Cats roster, so Sunday alone added about 30 percent to his season total. The House Cats entered at 6-12 on a two-game losing streak, and their 101.4 sits 7.4 points below the current median. Jeremy came into the matchup with a 3-1 all-time record against Luke.

Jahmyr Gibbs had the second-best game, 40.7 points, and his team is in better shape. Josh's Lisan al Gibbs leads The Silly Geese 125.5 to 115.0. Gibbs entered the week with 192.2 points in eight starts, the top total on the league's best team, and Lisan al Gibbs has one starter, Zay Flowers, still to play Monday.

Patrick Mahomes scored 35.4 for Bryar's The Mouse Rats, more than the 33.0 he had produced in three starts for them since arriving from The Silly Geese in an October 16 trade. The Mouse Rats trail Breece's Pieces 105.7 to 100.7 with Derrick Henry still to play.

Emmett Johnson's 32.1 points may be the most surprising line of the day. Garrett's Every Inch Matters acquired him from The Silly Geese on October 2 in a deal that also brought Michael Wilson and Jordyn Tyson, and through Week 9 Johnson had not started a game for his new team. He scored 22.8 on the bench in Week 8. This time he was in the lineup, and Every Inch Matters leads Real Man of Genius 119.2 to 75.0.

stories.headline: Two-Tenths of a Point Separate Sixth and Seventh in Week 10 Projections
stories.dek: Breece's Pieces is projected just above Pteem Shteevenshun for the last median win, while Every Inch Matters eyes a jump into sixth place.
body: The median game could come down to the smallest of margins this weekend. Heading into Sunday, Tyler's Breece's Pieces is projected for 102.0 points and Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun for 101.8, sixth and seventh in the league. Less than two-tenths of a point separates the last projected median win from the first projected median loss.

The top of the projected order looks more settled. The Silly Geese lead at 131.6, followed by Illegal use of hands at 120.1, Lisan al Gibbs at 117.4, GAYleb williams at 113.2 and Every Inch Matters at 110.4. Below the line, The Mouse Rats are projected for 97.5, I want my Nickleback for 93.3, After Bowers for 92.5, Real Man of Genius for 91.4 and The House Cats for 87.3. Weekly medians this season have ranged from 91.8 in Week 2 to 116.2 in Week 5.

The numbers matter most in the race for sixth. After Bowers holds that seed at 8-10, level with The Mouse Rats, and both are projected to lose head to head and finish below the median. Ezra's team visits GAYleb williams, projected to lose 113.2 to 92.5, though Ezra is 3-1 against Landon all time. The Mouse Rats visit Breece's Pieces, projected to lose 102.0 to 97.5, with Bryar 3-0 against Tyler.

Garrett has the clearest path to move up. Every Inch Matters hosts Real Man of Genius and is projected to win 110.4 to 91.4. Garrett leads Micah 6-4 in their series, the most meetings of any pairing this week. A two-win week would lift Every Inch Matters to 9-11, and if every projection held, Garrett would sit alone in sixth, a game ahead of After Bowers and The Mouse Rats, with Real Man of Genius falling to 7-13.

Caleb's team is the most exposed to the margin. Pteem Shteevenshun is projected to beat I want my Nickleback 101.8 to 93.3, despite trailing 20.8 to 7.2 after Thursday night, and the median game would decide whether it finishes the week 8-12 or 7-13. Breece's Pieces has won its last three head-to-head games and has averaged 114.7 points over the last three weeks, third-best in the league.

stories.headline: Skattebo's Thursday Puts The Silly Geese Ahead of Lisan al Gibbs
stories.dek: Michael's team banked 25.7 points on Thursday and is projected to hand the 16-2 league leaders their second head-to-head loss of the season.
body: The week's biggest matchup already has a leader. Cam Skattebo scored 25.7 points on Thursday night, the best individual score from the early games, and Michael's The Silly Geese lead Josh's Lisan al Gibbs 25.7 to 0. The Silly Geese are projected to win 131.6 to 117.4, the highest projected total of any team this week.

Skattebo came to Michael from Bryar's The Mouse Rats in an Oct. 16 trade that sent Patrick Mahomes and Omarion Hampton the other way. Skattebo scored 46.3 points as a Mouse Rats starter before the deal and had 0 points in his one start for The Silly Geese through Week 9. Mahomes has 33 points in three starts for his new team.

Lisan al Gibbs has been the league's steadiest team. At 16-2, Josh is 8-1 head to head and 8-1 against the median, and his only head-to-head loss came in Week 4, 126.9 to 97.4 against GAYleb williams. His team has allowed 806.4 points, the fewest in the league, and posted the season's highest single score, 162.6 in Week 5. Jahmyr Gibbs leads the roster with 192.2 points in eight starts, and Matthew Stafford has 142.9 in nine.

Michael's lineup is built around the top-scoring player on any roster. Josh Allen has 200.2 points in eight starts, and CeeDee Lamb has 166.8 in nine. The Silly Geese are 12-6 and hold the third seed, with a 6-3 mark both head to head and against the median. A score of 131.6 would be the team's third-highest of the season, behind 144.4 in Week 1 and 133.2 in Week 2.

The all-time series between the two managers is tied 3-3. Josh leads Jeremy's Illegal use of hands by three games for the top seed, and Jeremy is projected to beat The House Cats 120.1 to 87.3. If the projections held, Lisan al Gibbs would still win its median game as the week's third-highest scorer, and the lead at the top would shrink to two games, 17-3 to 15-5. The Silly Geese would move to 14-6. Next week, Josh visits Breece's Pieces, a series tied 3-3.

stories.headline: Jayden Daniels Gives I want my Nickleback a Head Start on Caleb
stories.dek: Jared's team leads Pteem Shteevenshun 20.8 to 7.2 going into Sunday in a series Jared leads 4-3, though Caleb is still projected to win.
body: Jared's I want my Nickleback has not won a head-to-head game since Week 5, but it takes a lead into Sunday. Jayden Daniels scored 20.8 points on Thursday night, accounting for all of the team's total so far, and Jared leads Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun 20.8 to 7.2. Austin Ekeler produced all 7.2 for Caleb.

The projections still favor Pteem Shteevenshun, 101.8 to 93.3. Jared leads the all-time series 4-3. Daniels arrived in a Sept. 29 trade with Garrett and has 82.8 points in four starts, the most of anyone on Jared's roster. Ekeler was one of Caleb's two $7 waiver claims this week, the largest bids of Week 10.

Jared has had a difficult season after winning the 2024 title. At 3-15, I want my Nickleback is 2-7 head to head and 1-8 against the median, and its only median win came in Week 1, when it scored 129.1 to beat Every Inch Matters. The team has lost four straight head-to-head games and finished below the median five weeks running. Jared has made eight trades, the most in the league, and has spent his full $100 FAAB budget.

Caleb's 6-12 record understates his team's scoring. Pteem Shteevenshun has 960.4 points, fifth-most in the league, and has allowed 960.2. It lost the season's closest game, 97.7 to 97.2 to Real Man of Genius in Week 8, and fell 136.9 to 135.5 to Illegal use of hands in Week 3. Last week it posted the league's best score, 138.7, led by Jordan Love's 36.2.

Two other games began Thursday. The House Cats lead Illegal use of hands 22.0 to 0 behind J.J. McCarthy's 17.1 and Malik Nabers' 4.9, though Jeremy is projected to win 120.1 to 87.3 and leads Luke 3-1 all time. Real Man of Genius has 9.7 against Every Inch Matters, 5.7 of them from Rachaad White. Breece's Pieces against The Mouse Rats and GAYleb williams against After Bowers have yet to start.

stories.headline: Josh Adds C.J. Stroud, Then Draws the Team That Traded Him
stories.dek: Lisan al Gibbs sent Zach Charbonnet to The Silly Geese on Nov. 10, and the two meet this week with the Dec. 2 deadline 20 days off.
body: The league's newest trade comes with a rematch built in. On Nov. 10, Josh's Lisan al Gibbs acquired quarterback C.J. Stroud from Michael's The Silly Geese for running back Zach Charbonnet. This week the two teams play each other, with the 16-2 league leaders projected to win 117.8 to 105.5 and the managers' all-time series tied 3-3.

Michael claimed Stroud for $26 on Oct. 21, the fourth-largest FAAB bid of the season. With Josh Allen at quarterback, Stroud rarely saw the lineup. Allen has 200.2 points in eight starts, the most of anyone on the roster, and Stroud started once, scoring 16.5. His best week came on the bench, where he scored 35.4 in Week 9.

On Josh's side, Matthew Stafford has started all nine weeks and scored 142.9 points, and Bo Nix put up 15.7 as a reserve in Week 9. Charbonnet never started for Lisan al Gibbs, whose backfield is led by Jahmyr Gibbs, with 192.2 points in eight starts, and D'Andre Swift, with 141.8 in nine. Josh also claimed Kaleb Johnson for $4 this week.

It is Josh's second deal in two weeks. On Oct. 29 he landed Tee Higgins from Jared, and Higgins has 50.2 points in two starts for his new team, including 32.5 in Week 8, the top individual score that week. Josh sent back DK Metcalf, who had 60.5 points as his starter, and Ollie Gordon II, his $55 claim from Week 4 and the largest bid of the season. Gordon has 13.8 points in two starts for Jared.

Michael has now made six trades, second only to Jared's eight. Results have varied: Michael Wilson, sent to Garrett on Oct. 2, has 63.9 points in six starts for Every Inch Matters, while A.J. Brown has 10.5 in two starts for The Silly Geese. At 12-6, Michael's team holds the third seed, one game ahead of GAYleb williams and Breece's Pieces, and Josh leads Illegal use of hands by three games for the top spot.

stories.headline: Caleb Leads Week 10 Waivers With $7 Bids on Austin Ekeler and Konata Mumpfield
stories.dek: Pteem Shteevenshun made the week's two biggest claims, adding to a waiver record that already includes the season's best pickup.
body: No one bid more on this week's waiver wire than Caleb. Pteem Shteevenshun claimed running back Austin Ekeler and receiver Konata Mumpfield for $7 apiece, the two largest bids of Week 10. Micah followed with $6 for the Commanders D/ST, dropping Michael Mayer, and Josh spent $4 each on Kaleb Johnson and Tutu Atwell, letting Rashid Shaheed go.

The rest of the claims came cheap. Jared paid $2 for Pat Bryant and dropped Kimani Vidal, and Jeremy spent $1 on the 49ers D/ST. Michael made three claims at no cost: the Colts D/ST, tight end Chig Okonkwo, for whom he dropped Brian Thomas Jr., and kicker Evan McPherson. Luke added Fernando Mendoza as a free agent and released Brandon Aiyuk.

Caleb has a track record on the wire. His $23 claim on Jordan Love in Week 6 tops the season's list of pickups that paid off, with 94.9 points in four starts, including 36.2 in Week 9, the best individual score of that week. Spencer Shrader, a free pickup, is second on that list with 83 points in seven starts. Those additions help explain why Pteem Shteevenshun has scored 960.4 points, fifth-most in the league, despite a 6-12 record.

Jeremy has done well with small bets, too. Jared Goff, a $5 claim, has 71.6 points in four starts for Illegal use of hands, and kicker Chris Boswell, a free pickup, has 69 in seven. Ezra's $7 claim on the Vikings D/ST has returned 53 points in four starts, and Tyler's free pickup of Jason Myers has 52 in six.

The biggest bids have been less certain. Josh's $55 on Ollie Gordon II never produced a start before Gordon was traded. Jared has spent $97 of his $100 budget, the most in the league, ahead of Ezra at $91 and Garrett at $86, while Jeremy has spent $30, the least. Garrett has made 77 pickups, the most of any team, with Bryar next at 52 and Ezra at 43.

stories.headline: No Trades, Little FAAB: Jeremy and Landon Built Contenders by Holding Firm
stories.dek: Illegal use of hands and GAYleb williams have yet to make a trade and have spent the least FAAB, yet rank second and third in power.
body: With the trade deadline 20 days away, three teams have not made a single trade, and two of them sit near the top of the league. Jeremy's Illegal use of hands, at 13-5, and Landon's GAYleb williams, at 11-7, rank second and third in the power rankings. They have also spent the least FAAB of any teams, $30 and $32.

Jeremy's roster has carried the league's best offense. Illegal use of hands has scored 1,121.7 points, 124.6 per week, both league highs. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 196.6 points in nine starts, Kyren Williams 141.1 in nine and Puka Nacua 138.6 in seven. The team posted the week's high score three weeks running, from Week 6 through Week 8, peaking at 148.9. This week it hosts The House Cats, projected to win 118.6 to 108.1, and Jeremy leads Luke 3-1 all time.

Landon has made only eight pickups, tied with Tyler for the fewest. His one big bid was $30 on Bryce Young in Week 3, the third-largest of the season. The lineup has been led by Javonte Williams, with 130.3 points in eight starts, Amon-Ra St. Brown, with 127.1 in eight, and Chuba Hubbard, with 111.4 in seven. GAYleb williams has allowed 860.0 points, second-fewest behind Lisan al Gibbs, and has the easiest remaining schedule, with opponents averaging 96.4 points per game.

Neither manager has a title yet. Jeremy was the top seed in 2025 at 20-8 and finished runner-up to Tyler, his only playoff trip in three past seasons. Landon reached the playoffs as the sixth seed in 2024 and finished fifth, and is 18-24 across two past seasons. This week he hosts After Bowers, projected to win 113.4 to 95.7, though Ezra leads the all-time series 3-1.

The third team without a trade is Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun, which has relied on the waiver wire instead. Elsewhere, the busiest front offices have mixed results: Jared has made eight trades and sits 3-15, while Michael has made six and holds the third seed at 12-6.

stories.headline: Six Winners, Six Median Wins as Week 9 Splits the League Down the Middle
stories.dek: Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun posted the top score, 138.7, and every head-to-head winner also finished above the 105.1 median.
body: Week 9 drew an unusually clean line through the league. All six head-to-head winners also posted the week's six highest scores, so half the teams went 2-0 and the other half went 0-2. Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun led the way with 138.7 points, its best total of the season, in a 138.7 to 90.7 win over The House Cats.

Jordan Love carried that game with 36.2 points, the best individual score of the week, and Bijan Robinson added 23.7. Christian McCaffrey scored 21.7 for Luke's side, but the 48.0-point margin was the widest of the week. The result lifted Pteem Shteevenshun from ninth to seventh in the power rankings, the biggest climb of any team.

Tyler's Breece's Pieces beat The Silly Geese 124.2 to 97.3. Joe Burrow started and scored 29.5, with Drake Maye's 18.3 left on the bench, and Ja'Marr Chase added 26.5. Breece's Pieces have now won three straight head-to-head games and cleared the median in each of those weeks. Michael got 28.5 from CeeDee Lamb, while C.J. Stroud scored 35.4 on his bench, the most by any reserve in the league.

Landon's GAYleb williams handled The Mouse Rats 111.4 to 83.5 behind 20.4 points from Javonte Williams. Every Inch Matters beat After Bowers 113.7 to 103.6 as Kenneth Walker III scored 34.3 and Brock Purdy 25.3. Lisan al Gibbs topped I want my Nickleback 113.7 to 79.3, with Christian Watson scoring 26.6; Josh's team finished 0.04 points ahead of Garrett's for the week. Jared's 79.3 was the week's low score.

The upset belonged to Micah. Real Man of Genius beat Illegal use of hands 106.5 to 99.7 and took the sixth and final median spot. After Bowers, at 103.6, missed it by 2.9 points. The median itself has climbed every week since Week 6 and reached 105.1, its highest mark since Week 5.

stories.headline: One Playoff Spot, Six Teams: The Race for Sixth Tightens
stories.dek: After Bowers and The Mouse Rats are tied at 8-10, with Every Inch Matters and Real Man of Genius one game back after two-win weeks.
body: Five weeks and 10 games remain, and the fight for the last playoff spot now runs six teams deep. After Bowers holds the sixth seed at 8-10, level with The Mouse Rats after both went 0-2 in Week 9. Every Inch Matters and Real Man of Genius closed to 7-11 with two-win weeks, and Pteem Shteevenshun and The House Cats sit at 6-12.

Above the line, the top five have some room. Lisan al Gibbs is 16-2, Illegal use of hands 13-5 and The Silly Geese 12-6, while GAYleb williams and Breece's Pieces are both 11-7, three games clear of seventh place. The week also widened the race for the top seed: Josh's lead over Jeremy grew from one game to three.

Ezra's After Bowers has leaned on the median all season. It is 3-6 head-to-head but 5-4 against the median, and its 923.2 points are the most among the six bubble teams except Pteem Shteevenshun. The schedule may help, too. After Bowers' remaining opponents average 98.6 points per game, the second-easiest slate in the league. Every Inch Matters has the hardest, with opponents averaging 109.1.

Pteem Shteevenshun's record hides its scoring. Caleb's team has 960.4 points, fifth-most in the league and more than Breece's Pieces, and its 111.9-point average over the last three weeks ranks fourth. It has also allowed 960.2, almost exactly what it has scored. The House Cats, at 869.3 points, need to make up the same two games.

Week 10 puts two bubble teams head to head. Every Inch Matters hosts Real Man of Genius, with Garrett leading Micah 6-4 all time and projected to win 105.5 to 86.0. After Bowers visits GAYleb williams, which is projected ahead 112.1 to 94.9, though Ezra is 3-1 against Landon. The Mouse Rats visit Breece's Pieces with a 96.1 to 92.7 projected edge, and Bryar is 3-0 against Tyler. Pteem Shteevenshun is projected to beat I want my Nickleback 101.9 to 86.9, and The House Cats visit Illegal use of hands, projected 108.2 to 95.8 against them.

stories.headline: Micah's Season-High 106.5 Ends Jeremy's Six-Game Winning Run
stories.dek: Real Man of Genius beat Illegal use of hands by 6.8 points, handing the league's top-scoring team its first head-to-head loss since Week 2.
body: Real Man of Genius delivered the surprise of Week 9. Micah's team beat Illegal use of hands 106.5 to 99.7, its highest score of the season, and ended Jeremy's run of six straight head-to-head wins. It was only the second time all season that Jeremy's team finished below the median, and the first since Week 2.

Matthew Golden led Micah's lineup with 27.4 points and Tyler Shough added 19.7. The win was the second straight for Real Man of Genius, which beat Pteem Shteevenshun 97.7 to 97.2 in Week 8, the closest game of the season. The 106.5 also earned the team its third median win of the year.

Jeremy got 28.0 from Puka Nacua and 17 from kicker Dominic Zvada, a free-agent pickup on Nov. 4. The bench held more: Tank Dell scored 18.5 there, while Jameson Williams scored 4.5 in the lineup. The 99.7 was Illegal use of hands' lowest total since Week 2 and its first score under 100 since then.

The loss cost Jeremy ground at the top. Illegal use of hands still leads the league with 1,121.7 points, ahead of Lisan al Gibbs at 1,105.0, but it has also allowed 994.0, third-most in the league. Josh's team has allowed 806.4, the fewest. Lisan al Gibbs moved past it to No. 1 in the power rankings, 88.2 to 86.0, and is now three games ahead of 13-5 Illegal use of hands with 10 games left.

For Micah, the win kept Real Man of Genius one game behind sixth at 7-11. Two of its starters arrived in a Week 3 trade with Tyler: Travis Kelce has 40.7 points in five starts and Aaron Jones Sr. 40.1 in four. The next test is a trip to Every Inch Matters, where Garrett leads the series 6-4. Jeremy hosts The House Cats, holding a 3-1 all-time edge over Luke.

stories.headline: Projections Put Three Bottom-Half Teams Above This Week's Median Line
stories.dek: The House Cats, Pteem Shteevenshun and Every Inch Matters are all projected into the top six, with After Bowers and The Silly Geese on the outside.
body: The median game could reshuffle the middle of the standings this weekend. Week 9 projections place The House Cats (120.1), Pteem Shteevenshun (114.7) and Every Inch Matters (114.6), three teams with losing records, among the week's six highest scores, while playoff contenders Breece's Pieces, The Silly Geese and After Bowers sit just below the cut.

Illegal use of hands leads the projections at 123.9, followed by Lisan al Gibbs at 122.6, The House Cats at 120.1 and GAYleb williams at 117.1. The fight for the last two spots could hardly be tighter on paper: Pteem Shteevenshun is projected only 0.04 points ahead of Every Inch Matters. Breece's Pieces is next at 109.1, 5.5 points short of sixth, with I want my Nickleback at 107.0, The Silly Geese at 104.4 and After Bowers at 103.8.

The stakes are highest for Ezra. After Bowers holds the sixth seed at 8-8 with a 3-5 head-to-head record, so its 5-3 mark against the median has done most of the work, and The Mouse Rats are level at 8-8 behind it. Tyler's Breece's Pieces, at 9-7, is 4-4 against the median. Michael's Silly Geese are 6-2 against it but have averaged 98.3 points over the last three weeks, down from 114.9 for the season.

For the teams projected to crash the top six, a median win would be a rare one. Every Inch Matters and Pteem Shteevenshun are each 2-6 against the median, and The House Cats are 3-5. Garrett's team scored 87.5 last week but is projected for 114.6 against After Bowers, which leads that game 10.2 to 0 so far.

The line itself has moved a lot. Weekly medians have ranged from 91.8 in Week 2 to 116.2 in Week 5, and last week's was 100.7. Five teams already have points on the board: Lisan al Gibbs with 20.8, The Mouse Rats with 18.7, The House Cats with 12.0, After Bowers with 10.2 and Illegal use of hands with 8.9. The other seven have yet to score.

stories.headline: Luke and Caleb Meet With a Possible Two-Win Week on the Line
stories.dek: The House Cats lead Pteem Shteevenshun 12.0 to 0, and both teams are projected to finish above the median.
body: The game between The House Cats and Pteem Shteevenshun pairs two teams below .500, but it may carry more weight than any other on the schedule for the winner. Both are projected to clear the median, which means one side could leave the week with two wins. Luke's team leads 12.0 to 0 on the strength of the Jaguars D/ST, and projections favor it 120.1 to 114.7.

The House Cats are 6-10, two games behind After Bowers for the sixth seed with 12 games left, median games included. They have played some of their best football lately, averaging 105.2 points over the last three weeks, third-best in the league behind Illegal use of hands and Lisan al Gibbs. That stretch included wins over I want my Nickleback and The Silly Geese before a 135.5 to 96.2 loss to Lisan al Gibbs last week. Christian McCaffrey leads the roster with 127.0 points in seven starts, and the Jaguars D/ST followed a 21-point Week 8 with 12 more already this week.

Caleb's record undersells his team's scoring. Pteem Shteevenshun is 4-12, yet its 821.7 points rank fifth in the league. It owns the two narrowest losses of the season, 136.9 to 135.5 against Illegal use of hands in Week 3 and 97.7 to 97.2 against Real Man of Genius last week, plus a 3.6-point loss to The Mouse Rats in Week 6. Bijan Robinson (140.8) and Jonathan Taylor (133.7) have been steady all year, and Spencer Shrader, a free pickup, has 67 points in six starts.
Both managers worked the wire this week. Luke claimed J.J. McCarthy for $9 and added Brandon Aiyuk. Caleb picked up Hunter Henry and the Buccaneers D/ST.

The all-time series is even at 2-2. Caleb has reached the playoffs in two of his three past seasons, finishing fourth in 2024 and fifth in 2025. Luke is still looking for his first trip, and a two-win week would pull The House Cats to 8-10 with five weeks to play.

stories.headline: Jared Keeps Reworking His Roster as Lisan al Gibbs Comes to Town
stories.dek: The 2024 champion has made seven trades and spent $95 in FAAB, both league highs, and gets the 14-2 leaders this week.
body: No manager has been busier than Jared. His I want my Nickleback has made seven trades, the most in the league, and spent $95 in FAAB, also the most, while making 33 pickups. The 2024 champion is 3-13 and has lost seven straight, and this week brings the top-seeded Lisan al Gibbs, which leads 20.8 to 0 with Cam Little already scoring 17 points.

Some of the deals have produced. Jayden Daniels, acquired from Garrett in Week 3, has 68.2 points in three starts for Jared, and J.K. Dobbins, part of a Week 5 deal with Michael, has 34.8 in three starts. Jalen Coker, from Ezra in Week 3, has added 22.7. Others have gone the other way: Kenneth Walker III has 75.4 points in four starts for Garrett since leaving in that Week 3 trade, and Alvin Kamara has 35.8 in three starts for After Bowers.

The roster keeps circling back to familiar names. Jared and Garrett traded Kyler Murray and Kendre Miller to each other on Oct. 20, then reversed the swap eight days later. This week, Jared claimed Kyle Pitts Sr. for $5, the tight end he had sent to Ezra in Week 3, and dropped Juwan Johnson, who had arrived in that same deal. He also added Nicholas Singleton, the Bills D/ST and Elijah Mitchell.

The results have yet to follow. I want my Nickleback has scored 720.8 points, second-fewest in the league, and is 1-7 against the median, its lone median win coming in a 129.1-point Week 1. Its last head-to-head win came in Week 5, 82.6 to 55.6 over Real Man of Genius.

Jared does hold a 2-1 all-time edge over Josh, whose team is 14-2 and projected to win 122.6 to 107.0. That projection would leave I want my Nickleback 7.6 points shy of the current median cut, close enough that a strong weekend could snap the losing streak in at least one of its two games.

stories.headline: Two-Time Champion Tyler Gets His Shot at Michael's Silly Geese
stories.dek: Breece's Pieces are projected favorites against the No. 3 seed, though Tyler trails Michael 3-5 in their all-time series.
body: The weekend's marquee game puts the league's only two-time champion against the No. 3 seed. Tyler's Breece's Pieces (9-7) host Michael's Silly Geese (12-4), neither side has scored a point yet, and the projections lean toward the home team, 109.1 to 99.2. It is the first meeting of the season between the two.

History favors Michael, who holds a 5-3 edge in the all-time series. The 2023 season ended with Tyler as champion and Michael as runner-up, and Tyler added a second title in 2025. Michael is still chasing his first; his only playoff trip in three past seasons came in that 2023 run.

Breece's Pieces arrive on a climb. They jumped from ninth to sixth in the power rankings after beating GAYleb williams 118.0 to 103.7 in Week 8, with Ja'Marr Chase scoring 25.6 and Drake Maye 22.5. Bucky Irving leads the roster with 121.6 points in eight starts. The bench has been productive as well: Joe Burrow, acquired from Micah in a Week 3 trade, scored 28.9 in Week 7 and 39.5 in Week 8 without starting.

The Silly Geese have cooled from their early pace. They average 114.9 points a week but 98.3 over the last three, a stretch that included losses to Real Man of Genius and The House Cats before a 111.6 to 87.7 win over I want my Nickleback last week. Josh Allen remains the engine, with 187.3 points in seven starts and 26.6 last week. Michael, who has made five trades and 31 pickups, went back to waivers this week for Devin Singletary, Dylan Sampson, Brian Thomas Jr. and the Bears D/ST.

The stakes run in both directions. The Silly Geese sit four games clear of seventh place with six weeks left, and a win would help them keep pace with the top two seeds. Breece's Pieces are one game above the 8-8 pair of After Bowers and The Mouse Rats, and their remaining opponents average 109.3 points per game, the toughest slate among the league's top eight. Next week brings The Mouse Rats, a team Tyler is 0-3 against all time.

stories.headline: Jeremy Keeps Posting the Week's Top Score, but Josh Still Holds No. 1
stories.dek: Illegal use of hands has led the league in scoring three weeks running and sits one game behind 14-2 Lisan al Gibbs.
body: Jeremy's Illegal use of hands has posted the league's highest score in three consecutive weeks, 148.9, 126.9 and 136.6, and sits first in the power rankings. It still has not caught Lisan al Gibbs. Josh's team is 14-2, one game ahead of Jeremy at 13-3, and both carry early leads into the weekend against teams near the bottom of the standings.

Jeremy has won every head-to-head matchup since Week 3, when he edged Pteem Shteevenshun by 1.5 points. His 1,022.0 points are the most in the league, and his 137.5-point average over the last three weeks is nearly 22 points better than anyone else's. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 188.0 points as a starter, the top total on any roster, with Kyren Williams at 133.5 and Bhayshul Tuten at 110.8.

The gap comes down to opposing scores. Jeremy has allowed 887.5 points, second-most in the league, while Josh has allowed 727.1, the fewest by almost 50. Lisan al Gibbs has done plenty on its own end, too, with 991.2 points, second only to Jeremy. Its only losses came in Week 4, when GAYleb williams won 126.9 to 97.4 and the score also fell below the median.

Josh has kept building. He traded DK Metcalf and Ollie Gordon II to Jared for Tee Higgins in Week 8, and Higgins scored 32.5 in his first start, the best individual score of the week. Metcalf had produced 60.5 points for Josh before the deal and scored 0.9 in his debut for Jared. Gordon had cost Josh $55 in FAAB in Week 4, still the largest bid of the season. This week Josh claimed Bo Nix for $8.

Both leaders are in good shape for Week 9. Josh leads Jared's I want my Nickleback 20.8 to 0 after Cam Little scored 17.0, and the projection favors him 124.2 to 106.9, though Jared is 2-1 against Josh all time. Jeremy leads Micah's Real Man of Genius 8.9 to 0 on Bhayshul Tuten's early points and is projected to win 124.0 to 91.7. Next week, Josh hosts The Silly Geese while Jeremy hosts The House Cats.

stories.headline: Four Teams Within One Game Fight for the Last Three Playoff Spots
stories.dek: GAYleb williams meets The Mouse Rats, After Bowers visits Every Inch Matters, and The House Cats try to climb back from 6-10.
body: Below the top three, the playoff race is packed tight. GAYleb williams and Breece's Pieces are 9-7, After Bowers and The Mouse Rats are 8-8, and only three of those four can finish in a playoff seed if the standings hold. With six weeks and 12 games left, median games included, Week 9 puts two of them head to head.

Landon's GAYleb williams hosts Bryar's The Mouse Rats in a series tied 2-2 all time. The Mouse Rats lead 18.7 to 0 so far, with Parker Washington scoring 13.1 and Derrick Henry 5.6, but GAYleb williams is projected to win 117.0 to 96.2. Landon's team has the fourth-most points in the league at 877.1 and the softest remaining schedule, with opponents averaging 96.2 points per game.

The Mouse Rats come in after their toughest stretch of the season. They scored 66.7 in Week 8, the lowest total of the week, while Patrick Mahomes put up 25.4 on the bench, and they slid from fifth to eighth in the power rankings. Their 79.4-point average over the last three weeks is the lowest in the league. Bryar was active on the wire, adding Xavier Worthy, Sione Vaki and the Lions D/ST.

Ezra's After Bowers holds the sixth seed largely through the median game. Its head-to-head record is 3-5, but it is 5-3 against the median, and it moved from sixth to fifth in the power rankings.
